s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain, and muscle weakness with elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin
salient_findings: Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase) and bilirubin
Pancreatic head mass with associated pancreatic ductal dilatation
key_facts: 71-year-old man presented with three weeks of jaundice
Weight loss and abdominal pain
Bilateral lower-extremity weakness
No history of autoimmune or neuromuscular conditions
Taking atorvastatin as a home medication
Jaundice and significant scleral icterus on physical examination
Epigastric tenderness without guarding or rebound
Mild weakness in bilateral hip flexor muscles
Elevated AST (2536 IU/L) and ALT (919 IU/L)
Elevated total bilirubin (169.3 μmol/L)
Elevated alkaline phosphatase (894 IU/L)
Elevated creatinine (415.5 μmol/L) with a baseline of 70.7 μmol/L three months previously
Initial creatinine kinase (CK) level: 22,000 IU/L, later peaked at >40,000 IU/L
Pancreatic head mass with associated pancreatic ductal dilatation on CT abdomen/pelvis
Diffuse myositis affecting lower extremities on MRI

shortlist.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pancreatic head mass with associated pancreatic ductal dilatation and biliary stricture biopsy consistent with adenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated creatinine kinase (CK) level and right biceps femoris biopsy showing nonspecific myopathic changes consistent with rhabdomyolysis

shortlist.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Jaundice, elevated liver enzymes, and bilirubin, with a possible biliary stricture

shortlist.label: Statins-induced myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient taking atorvastatin and presenting with muscle weakness and elevated CK level

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse myositis affecting lower extremities on MRI and mild weakness in bilateral hip flexor muscles

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain, and a pancreatic head mass with associated pancreatic ductal dilatation on CT abdomen/pelvis, along with a biliary stricture biopsy consistent with adenocarcinoma, strongly supports this diagnosis. The elevated cancer antigen 19-9 level and genomic alterations in targeted regions of genes involved in biliary-tract malignancies further confirm this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyolysis
rejected.why: Although the patient has elevated creatinine kinase levels and myositis on MRI, these findings are likely secondary to the primary diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma, which can cause paraneoplastic syndromes including myositis.

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a biliary stricture biopsy consistent with adenocarcinoma, the pancreatic head mass and elevated cancer antigen 19-9 level are more suggestive of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Statins-induced myopathy
rejected.why: The patient's muscle weakness and elevated creatinine kinase levels could be attributed to statin use, but the presence of a pancreatic head mass and other findings suggest a more complex diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The patient's myositis on MRI could be consistent with polymyositis, but the presence of a pancreatic head mass and other findings suggest a paraneoplastic syndrome rather than a primary muscle disorder.
